analyse.explanation: ALL looks unusually expensive relative to TRV (z = +2.68), so the strategy would sell ALL and buy TRV.

evidence_cards.title: Move together
evidence_cards.how_this_works: We measure the Pearson correlation of the two stocks' daily percentage moves over the whole sample. Values near 1 mean they usually move in the same direction on the same day; this is only a first filter, never an edge.
evidence_cards.plain_english: The daily percentage moves of ALL and TRV lined up strongly.

evidence_cards.title: Stable enough relationship
detail_lines: Hedge ratio (beta): 0.699 (must be a positive, finite number)
Spread crossed its rolling average 62 times (minimum 6)
evidence_cards.how_this_works: Beta is the slope of the line of best fit between the two log prices: how much of B normally balances A. We check that it is positive, that it did not change dramatically while we were estimating it, that neither leg dominates the money, and that the spread genuinely oscillates around its average.
evidence_cards.plain_english: The line-of-best-fit relationship looks steady enough to use for a paper trade.

evidence_cards.title: Unusual today
evidence_cards.how_this_works: The z-score counts how many recent standard deviations today's spread sits from its previous 60-day average. It is a ruler for unusualness, not a prediction guarantee.
evidence_cards.plain_english: Today's gap is unusually wide: ALL looks expensive relative to TRV by about 2.7 recent standard deviations.

evidence_cards.title: Worked historically
detail_lines: Net profit after costs: +3.55% of gross exposure (must be > 0)
Total estimated costs: 1.22% of gross exposure
Limited evidence: 5-9 trades is too few to call reliable.
evidence_cards.how_this_works: We replay the identical fixed rule over the most recent 40% of dates, which were never used to fit the relationship. Signals form at a close, execute at the next open, and costs are charged on both legs at entry and exit. Passing this screen is a minimum requirement, not proof of future profit.
evidence_cards.plain_english: The unchanged rule cleared the minimum screen after costs, but with only 6 trades this is limited evidence, not statistical proof.

warnings: The historical screen passed with limited evidence (6 completed trades); treat the result with extra caution.

news_items.headline: Why Your Zip Code Is Uninsurable
news_items.snippet: One insurance company had zero losses in the 2025 LA fires. Meanwhile, State Farm, Allstate, and Farmers all pulled back coverage across the US. So what does this company know that 100-year-old insurers don't?*Want to know the other industries primed for disruption? We found them:* https://clickhubspot.com/a8ozTraditional home insurance prices risk by zip code — a system built for mail delivery, not wildfire prediction. That's why entire neighborhoods get flagged "uninsurable" even when some houses on the block would clearly survive a fire. A new wave of startups — Kettle, Delos, Kin — are throwing out the zip code model entirely, using satellite imagery, lidar, and AI to assess fire risk house by house. The results are wild: one model correctly predicted 97% of the homes that actually burned in California's wildfires, and another wrote 25,000 policies in fire-prone areas without a single loss in the Palisades and Eaton fires.
